# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut a wire. I need Mute to consult the manual and establish how Deaf’s visual observations can be communicated through gestures, then relay the relevant bomb details to me. I am sending a distinct gesture that Mute can define and explain to Deaf as a request for a complete report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile readings yet. Consult the manual and establish a gesture code so Deaf can report the display, light, and wire markings. Tell me the code and relay Deaf's observations to me. The gesture I am sending is a request for that report; please explain its meaning to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible bomb information: display 0. Indicator light red. Wires from left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

I now know the visible state through Deaf’s spoken report: display 0, red indicator, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. However, the correct wire still depends on the manual, which I have not received. I will ask Mute to provide the relevant rule; no physical action is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, red indicator, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Please send the manual rule for this exact state, including which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Please report every control and marking you can feel, including its order, shape, position, and any tactile labels.

I can feel no controls, labels, shapes, or markings beyond the three wire positions; the only permitted operation presented to me is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. I will report this to Mute so the information can be relayed to Deaf if needed, while still waiting for the manual rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel no controls, labels, shapes, or tactile markings. I can identify only three wire positions, left to right: 1, 2, and 3; the only permitted operation is cutting one of them. Please provide the manual rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible facts are known, but the manual rule is still missing. I have no additional tactile clue that can distinguish the wires, so cutting now would be an unjustified guess. I will ask Mute again for the exact rule and will not act until it is supplied.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The manual rule is still needed. For display 0, red light, and wires red-yellow-green, which position must I cut? Do not send a general procedure; send the exact position number.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled wire 1 using our agreed code. Do not cut or actuate anything yet; we still need the manual rule and your tactile control report.

Mute’s signal identifies wire 1, but Deaf reports that this is not yet confirmed by the manual. My tactile report is complete: there are only three selectable wire positions and no other controls or labels. I will request the exact manual rule again and continue to avoid cutting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I will not cut wire 1 yet. Please provide the exact manual rule or instruction that determines the cut for display 0, red light, and wire colors red-yellow-green, and confirm whether it selects position 1.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not cut anything yet. I am obtaining a yes-or-no authorization from the manual reader for wire 1.

Wire 1 is still not authorized; Deaf is obtaining confirmation from Mute. I will not cut anything without an explicit manual-based authorization. I am asking Mute to answer directly and unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer directly: does the manual authorize cutting wire position 1 for display 0, red light, and wires red-yellow-green? Reply exactly YES or NO, with the manual basis if NO.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The manual reader answered yes: cut wire 1. Wire 1 is the red wire. You may cut wire 1 now.

The manual reader has explicitly authorized cutting wire position 1 for the reported state, and Deaf confirms that position 1 is the red wire. I will now perform the authorized action.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
